bullets.title: S&P up 20% since March but 68% of gains concentrated in just 10 stocks
bullets.body: The S&P 500 has surged ~20% since end of March but the rally is described as 'insanely narrow' — just 10 stocks account for 68% of the advance. Tech was the only S&P 500 sector to outperform the index in May, and U.S. large-cap ETFs saw the largest inflows for another consecutive week while global ETFs faced outflows. Retail investors recorded their largest-ever single purchase of IGV this period.

bullets.title: CBOE Dispersion (DSPX) at 3rd-highest reading ever — single-stock vol divergence extreme
bullets.body: The CBOE DSPX dispersion index hit its 3rd highest reading in history, with only COVID 2020 and the April 2025 tariff episode producing higher readings. The index measures the ratio of S&P index implied vol to individual stock IV, signaling the market expects massive divergence between index-level calm and single-stock volatility. Separately, S&P correlation (COR1M) has fallen below 8, a level historically preceding 2-3% drawdowns as single-stock call positioning becomes overstretched.

bullets.title: GOOGL raises $80B for AI capex — hyperscaler spending now limited by market appetite, not cash
bullets.body: Alphabet launched an $80B capital raise comprising $15B common stock, $15B mandatory convertible preferred, a $10B private placement with Berkshire Hathaway at $351.81/Class A, and a $40B ATM commencing Q3 2026. GOOGL is down ~2.7-2.9% in premarket on dilution concerns. Analysts note this signals hyperscaler AI spending is now constrained by market financing capacity rather than internal cash generation, with 2027 capex potentially exceeding $300B — above Amazon's consensus $228B.

bullets.title: Barclays warns AI rally is 'increasingly vulnerable'; 22V sees momentum factor correction as technical, not fundamental
bullets.body: Barclays flags the AI-driven rally as showing signs of euphoria, crowded positioning, and rising interest-rate risks despite strong earnings. 22V Research characterizes recent AI beneficiary pullbacks as a Price Momentum factor correction, not fundamental deterioration, and recommends waiting to add AI capex baskets until momentum vol subsides. IGV rallied +45% since mid-April and +16% in 3 days, with forward valuations now implying 5-year EPS CAGR compression from 12% to 9%. 22V recommends hedging via IGV June puts and TLT July put spreads.

bullets.title: April JOLTS: 7.6M job openings beat sharply but 90% of surge concentrated in professional/business services
bullets.body: April JOLTS showed job openings jumping to 7.6M from 6.9M in March — the highest in two years — but Morgan Stanley notes 90% of the gain was concentrated in professional and business services, making the headline read artificially elevated. The vacancy rate jumped to 1.03 from 0.95 but lacks broad-based credibility. Layoff rates remain near cycle lows, quits ticked down to post-COVID lows, and the overall labor market is characterized as 'low hire, low fire.' The information sector showed tentative signs of higher churn, a possible early signal of AI boom broadening.

bullets.title: NFP Friday: JPM forecasts 75k vs Street 85k; SPX options pricing ~1% move
bullets.body: JPMorgan's desk expects May nonfarm payrolls of 75k (85k private) vs Street consensus of 85k and prior 115k, with unemployment seen holding at 4.3%. Options market is pricing ~1.0% SPX move for the June 5 expiry. A weaker print risks reigniting stagflation fears; a hotter print risks bond yield pressure. JPM's base case: 'economy is good and getting better.'

bullets.title: Eurozone CPI hits 3.2% YoY in May; ECB hike on 6/11 expected as 'insurance' move
bullets.body: Eurozone flash May CPI came in at 3.2% YoY (in line with estimates) with energy surging 11.0% YoY and services sticky at 3.5%. PSC macro projects acceleration to 4.7% by July due to the Iran War energy shock, supporting at least one ECB hike on June 11. ECB officials Rehn and Simkus both signaled timely action, with Rehn characterizing the June move as an 'insurance hike.' UBS warns that a less gradualist Fed under Warsh combined with ECB tightening into a slowing economy could be a policy error.

bullets.title: Global semiconductor market revised to $1.51T in 2026, up 90%; memory alone +250% to $800B+
bullets.body: WSTS sharply revised its global semiconductor market forecast to $1.51 trillion for 2026, up 90% and materially above the $1.0T estimate from March. Memory chips are expected to grow +250% to over $800B, while logic is up 37%. Americas region is forecast up 112%. SK Hynix's Chairman separately noted AI-driven memory shortages could persist through 2030, while SK Hynix plans to double wafer capacity over five years. Kioxia is seeking long-term NAND supply agreements with hyperscalers through 2029+.

bullets.title: AI is power-constrained, not compute-constrained — nuclear and grid plays emerging as next cycle leg
bullets.body: Multiple sources note that Jensen Huang and Elon Musk have both stated AI infrastructure is now power-bound rather than compute-bound. Nuclear operators (CEG 32GW, VST) and SMR developers (NuScale) are positioned as hyperscaler power solutions — Talen Energy already sold a 960MW nuclear campus to Amazon for $650M. Generac landed a hyperscaler backup power supply agreement, boosting FY27E EPS to $11.20 and putting $1B+ in large-MW data center revenue as the probable 2027 starting point.

bullets.title: White House AI executive order: cyber defense prioritized, NSA to benchmark frontier models within 60 days
bullets.body: The White House issued an executive order prioritizing cyber defense for National Security Systems within 30 days, directing CISA to establish federal AI-enabled cybersecurity tools and services, and tasking the NSA to develop a classified benchmarking process for 'covered frontier models' within 60 days. AI developers are invited into a voluntary framework for early model access and secure innovation partnerships. The order is broadly bullish for AI security vendors.

bullets.title: MSFT Build keynote today: Copilot super app, new reasoning model, NVDA CEO appearance; GitHub pricing causing 'sticker shock'
bullets.body: Microsoft's Build 2026 conference (12:30 PM ET) is expected to feature a Copilot super app launch, a new reasoning AI model, and an appearance by NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang. Separately, GitHub Copilot's new usage-based pricing is generating 'sticker shock' as users burn monthly caps in hours. A '#tokenmaxxing' trend is emerging — WMT, UBER, META, CRM, AMZN, and DASH are reportedly rationing AI tool usage per employee due to cost escalation. OpenAI Codex hit 5M+ weekly active users (+6x since February).

bullets.title: 22V macro regime: Normal expansion intact; inflation is the primary tail risk for sector rotation
bullets.body: 22V Research's quant macro model shows the economy remains in a 'Normal expansion' regime with credit spreads near historic lows and recession risk low. The 10-year yield fair value is pegged at 4.25-4.5%. The primary risk scenario is inflation: if core PCE rises 0.3% monthly through year-end, it would reach 3.8% YoY by end-2026, potentially triggering Fed tightening and driving rotation away from Semis/Tech Hardware toward Energy, Banks, and Insurance.

bullets.title: EM capital flows: Korea/India leading outflows; Korea exports +46% YoY cushioning oil shock
bullets.body: JPMorgan's EM Capital Flows Monitor shows the March quarter saw the largest net EM capital flow drop since March 2020, driven by foreign portfolio outflows from Korea and India. China is estimated to have seen $210B in capital outflows in 1Q26. Tech export surges (Korea +46% YoY) and metals prices are cushioning the oil price shock. Higher Treasury yields and a stronger dollar are expected to weigh on capital flow recovery.

bullets.title: ISM Manufacturing hits 4-year high in May; construction spending and April JOLTS beat
bullets.body: The ISM Manufacturing Index reached a four-year high in May, with new orders expanding for a fifth consecutive month and 16 industries reporting growth — the most since April 2022. April construction spending rose +0.4% MoM vs. +0.2% estimate, led by private residential +0.8%. These data points reinforce the 'Normal expansion' macro regime view.

bullets.title: Mid-June positioning risk: SpaceX IPO and June OpEx identified as logical catalyst for pullback
bullets.body: One macro/derivatives note identifies mid-June as a logical window for a positioning shift and potential pullback, citing the anticipated SpaceX IPO and June options expiration as catalysts. PDT restrictions lifting June 4 are expected to boost retail flow near-term. Vol Control Funds should continue mechanical buying as 1-month vol remains below 3-month vol. SPX 7,500 is flagged as a key technical support level.

bullets.title: IGV software ETF at vol extremes after +45% run; stock picking re-emerging within sector
bullets.body: Citi's Chart of the Day flags IGV at vol extremes after its unprecedented 3-day, 16% move. Intra-sector correlations declined during earnings season, making stock selection effective again within software. Upcoming earnings for PANW, CRWD, and ORCL (comprising ~24% of IGV) over the next 1.5 weeks represent a near-term volatility catalyst. DA Davidson separately warns the broad uniform IGV move misprices company-specific risks — bullish on DT, PEGA, PDFS, MANH; cautious on CRM, ASAN, SPSC.

bullets.title: Retail records largest-ever IGV purchase; passive flows amplifying mega-cap concentration
bullets.body: Retail investors made their largest-ever purchase of IGV this period. Passive indexing flows continue to concentrate in the same small set of mega-cap tech names that have driven the post-March rally, reinforcing the concentration risk flagged by multiple sources.

bullets.title: Consumer sentiment at all-time lows; 57% cite high prices as hurt to finances
bullets.body: Hedgeye retail data shows consumer sentiment hitting all-time lows, with 57% of consumers citing high prices as hurting their finances and personal savings rates at the lowest since 2022. A K-shaped economy is evident: lower-income consumers are most pressured, while upper-end spending continues. Gen Z survey data corroborates with 75% actively seeking lower-cost spending habits.

bullets.title: Geopolitical backdrop: Iran conflict repair faster than expected; oil pared gains on ceasefire signals
bullets.body: Iran's energy infrastructure repairs are progressing faster than expected following the conflict. Oil prices pared gains after Trump signaled efforts to broker an Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire. Iran has yet to respond to the U.S. nuclear proposal but is reviewing it. PSC macro still forecasts oil above $95/bbl through year-end even if the Strait of Hormuz reopens, sustaining the energy cost shock feeding into Eurozone CPI.

bullets.title: Anthropic confidentially filed for IPO; SpaceX IPO expected to be largest in U.S. history relative to GDP
bullets.body: Multiple sources note Anthropic has confidentially filed an S-1 for IPO with a valuation near $1T and ~$47B revenue run-rate. SpaceX's anticipated IPO is described as 'light-years' above any prior large IPO relative to U.S. GDP. The IPO pipeline (SpaceX, Anthropic, OpenAI) is expected to make 2026 a record year for offerings, though at least one market observer speculates the SpaceX IPO could be a catalyst for a market rerating lower given the magnitude of supply.
